newsitem.title: UK: Council votes grant to save Ayckbourn theatre.
newsitem.headline: Council votes grant to save Ayckbourn theatre.

text.p: Britain's best-loved playwright, Alan Ayckbourn, breathed a sigh of relief on Monday when councillors agreed to provide funds to save the theatre where all his works are premiered.
Ayckbourn had said he would have to close the Stephen Joseph Theatre in the English seaside resort of Scarborough unless the local authority agreed to help it further.
Councillors voted by 35 to nine to give the struggling playhouse an extra 50,000 pounds ($84,000) a year for five years, taking its grant to 200,000 pounds a year.
"The theatre is doing its best to balance its books," said council leader Mavis Don.
Ayckbourn is a prolific playwright whose past hits include Absurd Person Singular and the Norman Conquest trilogy.
His works are seldom absent from London's West End theatreland, being represented at present by By Jeeves, a musical written in collaboration with Andrew Lloyd Webber.
His success is getting more money for his Scarborough theatre came despite a refusal to flatter the resort.
"If you happen to be a teetotaller in this town God help you -- because there is little else to do apart from get drunk and buy shoes, it seems to me," he recently told a local newspaper.
